newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Boeing submits $4 billion order proposal to China.
newsitem.headline: Boeing submits $4 billion order proposal to China.

text.p: Boeing was submitting a number of proposals to China on Wednesday aimed at winning $4 billion worth of aircraft orders, according to Boeing's marketing vice-president, Bruce Dennis.

The move is being seen by some industry observers as a bid to trump rivals Airbus Industrie which is hoping a visit to Beijing by French President Jacques Chirac next month will clinch orders for up to 100 airliners worth $4 billion for the European consortium.
"Boeing is making a matrix of proposals covering a number of makes and models which we expect to deliver today," Dennis told reporters.

"We have been talking to all the Chinese airlines and the Chinese have asked for some different packages of proposals. But we are making proposals all the time so this is not something unique going on. We are very interested in the Chirac visit, like any manufacturer we would like everything, we would like it all but it probably won't happen. You will have to ask Li Peng what will happen but we are ready and we think our proposal is better," Dennis added.

He was in Hong Kong to present Boeing's current market outlook which predicts the world's highest air travel growth will be in the Asia-Pacific region over the next 20 years with a potential market for 4,400 jets worth $370 billion.
Air traffic growth rates in China are expected to be 10.3 per cent and Dennis described the Asia-Pacific market place as "an incredible battleground" as Boeing and Airbus fight for orders.
That fight has been hotting up recently. Boeing won an order for five B777-200 twin jets valued at around $685 million when U.S. vice president Al Gore met Premier Li Peng a month ago.

Boeing forecasts a total market of around 1,900 airliners worth $124 billion in China over the next 20 years. With between 70-80 orders per year, China will be the largest international commercial aircraft market, the company said. So far this year China has placed $1.13 billion worth of orders with Boeing, according to the company.
Dennis said the current US political argument over whether to grant China Most Favoured Nation (MFN) status to China had the potential to "definitely hurt us."

"Our position is: 'let's grant the MFN' We think it is better for China and the U.S. worker. Unfortunately we are one voice and Boeing does not have as much leverage in the US congress as some people think we do," Dennis said.
